A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIL/ASGDRO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison across the substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v2 reports original H-CMNIST and ASGDRO benchmark experiments, together with Grad-CAM and Hessian analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports revised benchmark outcomes, including ASGDRO combined with DPLCLIP on DomainNet.

M1.justification: The defining objective and Algorithm 1 change from v2's shared perturbation computed from pooled training loss to separate adversarial perturbations for each environment in v3. This revises a central optimization component. However, v3 Section 4.3 explicitly retains the shared-perturbation variant for every non-toy experiment, so this does not establish a corresponding change throughout the empirical implementation.

E1.justification: v3 adds DomainNet and its six domains to the existing DomainBed evaluation, under both training-domain and oracle model selection. Earlier dataset coverage remains represented: Multi-NLI and MetaShift survive in Appendix A.8, Figure 7, despite disappearing from their former main-text displays.

E2.justification: v3 adds PDE to three subpopulation comparisons and substantially expands WILDS comparisons with ERM/IRM and ERM, Bonsai and FeAT pretraining combinations. DomainBed replaces the backbone-oriented comparator list with domain-generalization methods, including GSAM, RDM, RS-SCM and LFME. Conversely, Multi-NLI retains GDRO but loses its ERM and ASAM comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported tuning settings change across both benchmark families. Subpopulation searches expand rho through 1.5, add gamma=0.1 and extend C through 5. DomainBed changes gamma's search range from 10^-2–1 to 10^-4–10^-2 and replaces the rho grid with {0.05, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0}. WILDS also adds explicit pretraining/fine-tuning comparison conditions. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The toy diagnostic testing whether ASGDRO penalizes sharp invariant directions is reported under per-environment perturbations in v3, whereas v2 specifies a shared pooled-loss perturbation. Its qualitative conclusion remains the same. H-CMNIST diagnostics, Grad-CAM examples and both Hessian analyses are otherwise retained; their relocation or recomposition does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: v3 first supplies uncertainty values for the subpopulation results in Table 5 and standard deviations for the WILDS/MetaShift comparison in Figure 7. Appendix A.6 newly specifies three seeds for H-CMNIST. The previously stated three-seed practice for subpopulation and DomainBed experiments remains; the PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Numerous subpopulation and DomainBed results change: ASGDRO's Waterbirds worst-group accuracy changes from 91.0% to 91.4%, while its VLCS training-domain-selection mean changes from 82.2 to 80.7. v3 adds DomainNet and expanded comparator results, but removes Multi-NLI average-accuracy and ERM/ASAM entries. Changed tuning and benchmark coverage prevent treating these as like-for-like performance gains or losses. H-CMNIST results and Hessian eigenvalues remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds formal definitions of invariance, invariant mechanisms and SIL, together with interpolation and feature-subset assumptions. Theorem 1 claims uniform mechanism weights under a squared-error setting; Proposition 1 connects the objective to gradient-norm regularization. Appendices A.2–A.5 add subset reasoning, proofs and a two-layer ReLU derivation for suppressing spurious features. v2 contains objectives and Gaussian toy mathematics but no comparable formal framework.

C1.justification: The central SIL, ASGDRO, H-CMNIST and distribution-shift robustness contributions remain. v3 adds the more specific claimed property that ASGDRO theoretically balances invariant mechanisms, and advertises formal theoretical guarantees in the abstract and conclusion. This extends the stated contribution beyond v2's empirical connection between flatness and diverse invariant features.

C2.justification: v3 develops a new account distinguishing rich feature representations from classifiers that actually use diverse invariant mechanisms, supported by its interpretation of the pretraining comparisons. Appendix A.5 adds a neuron-suppression explanation. Appendix A.1 newly acknowledges the two-pass computational cost and the limitations of validating SIL with synthetic H-CMNIST rather than richly annotated real-world data. v2's detailed rationale against separate group perturbations is removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports RTX A6000/RTX 3090 hardware and explicitly clarifies that H-CMNIST uses four class-by-box-position group losses. Conversely, it omits the detailed Multi-NLI training recipe and the JTT/SAM implementation links despite retaining Multi-NLI results. Most other dataset and implementation instructions, including LISA and DPLCLIP access links, remain.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around missing-feature generalization, rich representations, causal transfer and model interpolation. New discussions include Guo et al., Rojas-Carulla et al., Bonsai/FeAT-related work and Springer et al.'s balanced feature learning. These connections replace v2's broader claim that prior work had not connected flatness to general distribution shifts, while also supporting the new theoretical framework and comparator choices.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. The Gaussian example moves from methodology into experiments, benchmark discussions are consolidated, and Appendices A–D become A.1–A.11 with a new ordering. Terminology shifts toward environments and invariant mechanisms, and the author block is revised. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adds WILDS and uncertainty tables, restructures the DomainBed display, redraws schematic annotations and substantially rearranges the main-page layouts. The expanded WILDS chart and Waterbirds Hessian table move into the appendix. The main Grad-CAM figure is recomposed from existing appendix examples; the full appendix Grad-CAM panels and CelebA Hessian chart are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves uncertainty reporting, comparison breadth and explicit limitations. However, its main new guarantee has an unresolved step: Appendix A.4 introduces a mixture-weight penalty although the preceding squared-error gradient is weight-independent under the stated sum-to-one constraint. The theory also studies separate environment perturbations, while non-toy experiments retain the shared perturbation. These weaknesses in the strengthened theoretical claims make the net quality effect uncertain despite the documentation gains.
